section: Partition of Bengal 1905, Swadeshi and Boycott Movement; techniques and impact
subsections: Partition of Bengal - Viceroy, dates, stated vs real motives, annulment

accepted.s: The partition of Bengal in 1905 created which of the following administrative units and population distributions?
o: Eastern Bengal with 18 million people, and Western Bengal and Assam with 36 million people
Eastern Bengal and Assam with 54 million people, and the rest of Bengal with 31 million people
Eastern Bengal and Assam with 36 million people, and the rest of Bengal with 18 million people
Eastern Bengal and Assam with 31 million people, and the rest of Bengal with 54 million people
accepted.x: The partition created Eastern Bengal and Assam with 31 million people and the remaining Bengal with 54 million people.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive population figures to eliminate the reversed and recombined distributions.
accepted.sec: Partition of Bengal - Viceroy, dates, stated vs real motives, annulment  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the partition of Bengal, consider the following statements:
1. Administrative convenience was given as its official justification.
2. One of its political effects was to make Bengalis a minority in their own province.
3. Its underlying objective was to strengthen Bengali nationalism by uniting Hindus and Muslims.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Administrative convenience was the stated reason, while the actual policy sought to weaken Bengali nationalism and divide Hindus and Muslims. The third statement is therefore false.
accepted.tq: Separate the stated administrative justification from the political motive behind the measure.
accepted.sec: Partition of Bengal - Viceroy, dates, stated vs real motives, annulment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Moderate campaign against the partition of Bengal during 1903–1905?
o: It was led by Lord Curzon and relied mainly on official proclamations and military action.
It was led by Hardinge II and relied mainly on revolutionary violence and secret societies.
It was led by King George V and relied mainly on the boycott of constitutional institutions.
It was led by S.N. Banerjee, K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray and relied mainly on petitions and meetings.
accepted.x: The Moderates’ campaign from 1903 to 1905 was associated with S.N. Banerjee, K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray, and used petitions and meetings. The campaign failed to prevent the partition.
accepted.tq: Match the leaders with the characteristic constitutional methods rather than the later militant methods.
accepted.sec: Partition of Bengal - Viceroy, dates, stated vs real motives, annulment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: On 16 October 1905, the day on which the partition of Bengal came into effect, which of the following combinations was associated with the popular protest?
o: Industrial strike, salt march, individual satyagraha and underground revolt
Day of mourning, hartal, bathing in the Ganga and Rakhi-bandhan
National education, constitutional reform, separate electorates and provincial autonomy
Day of celebration, military parade, temple entry and public feasting
accepted.x: The day was observed as a day of mourning and hartal; people took a bath in the Ganga and observed Rakhi-bandhan as a symbol of unity.
accepted.tq: Identify the cluster of contemporaneous protest rituals linked to the effective date.
accepted.sec: Partition of Bengal - Viceroy, dates, stated vs real motives, annulment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The annulment of the partition of Bengal was announced at which event, and what important administrative change accompanied it?
o: The Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906; the capital was shifted from Delhi to Calcutta.
The Delhi Durbar of King George V in 1911; the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.
The Simla Conference of 1911; the capital was shifted from Delhi to Calcutta.
The Delhi Durbar of Edward VII in 1903; the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Bombay.
accepted.x: The partition was annulled on 12 December 1911 at the Delhi Durbar of King George V. The capital was simultaneously transferred from Calcutta to Delhi.
accepted.tq: Link the annulment event with its accompanying capital-transfer decision.
accepted.sec: Partition of Bengal - Viceroy, dates, stated vs real motives, annulment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who described Bengal as “the nerve centre of Indian nationalism” in the context of the partition of Bengal?
o: King George V
H.H. Risley
Lord Hardinge II
Lord Curzon
accepted.x: Lord Curzon described Bengal as “the nerve centre of Indian nationalism,” reflecting the political significance he attached to the province.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the Viceroy, the Home Secretary and the monarch associated with the episode.
accepted.sec: Partition of Bengal - Viceroy, dates, stated vs real motives, annulment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly explains why the partition of Bengal was regarded as a measure against Bengali nationalism?
o: It transferred all Bengali districts to a single enlarged province under one administration.
It divided the Bengali-speaking population and made Bengalis a minority in the remaining province.
It abolished the distinction between Eastern Bengal and Assam and the rest of Bengal.
It granted complete provincial autonomy to Bengal and ended official interference.
accepted.x: The partition separated Bengali-speaking areas and altered the demographic balance so that Bengalis became a minority in their own province, thereby weakening the nationalist centre in Bengal.
accepted.tq: Apply the demographic and political consequences to identify the measure’s real nationalist impact.
accepted.sec: Partition of Bengal - Viceroy, dates, stated vs real motives, annulment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: King George V — Viceroy who announced the partition of Bengal
Lord Hardinge II — Viceroy at the time of annulment
H.H. Risley — “Bengal united is a power”
Lord Curzon — Partition of Bengal
accepted.x: King George V was the monarch at whose Delhi Durbar the annulment was announced; he was not the Viceroy who announced the partition. Lord Curzon announced the partition, while Lord Hardinge II was Viceroy at the time of its annulment.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong authority by separating the monarch from the Viceroy who exercised executive authority.
